evidence: Scientist (Hopeton 'Overton' Brown) began working around King Tubby's Waterhouse studio as a teenager in the mid-1970s, first repairing equipment, and became one of Tubby's lead mixing engineers by the early 1980s; Tubby is widely credited as the source of his nickname. Documented in Wikipedia's article on Scientist and multiple reggae biography sources (AllMusic, Enkis Music).

later.title: Scientist Rids the World of the Evil Curse of the Vampires

trackPair.whatToListenFor: Tubby's own dub instrumentals treat the desk as an instrument played live, dropping instruments in and out and pushing the spring reverb hard. A decade later, mixing at the same studio, Scientist applies the identical toolkit, echo, filtering, sudden drop-outs, to a new decade's rhythms, with a themed album concept built on top.

explanation.age13: Scientist started out fixing King Tubby's equipment as a teenager and became one of his chief mixing engineers. His own dub albums in the early 1980s used the techniques he learned at Tubby's desk.
explanation.adult: A direct production and mentorship lineage inside a single studio: Scientist's early-1980s work is Tubby's toolkit carried forward by an engineer Tubby trained, applied to a new generation of Kingston bands after Tubby's own studio work had slowed.
